headline: Sales top plan and guidance raised despite GAAP profit dip
summary_short: Target's Q1 2026 net sales rose 6.7% y/y to $25,443M on 5.6% comparable-sales growth, but GAAP diluted EPS fell 24.5% y/y to $1.71 against a year-ago quarter that included $441M of non-recurring interchange-fee settlement gains; the company raised full-year 2026 net sales growth guidance to around 4%.
summary_long: Net sales grew 6.7% y/y to $25,443M on 5.6% comparable-sales growth (traffic +4.4%, digital +8.9%), with all six merchandise categories higher and non-merchandise revenue up nearly 25%. Gross margin rose to 29.0% from 28.2% on supply-chain productivity and lower markdowns, while SG&A rate rose to 21.9% on higher compensation, capital-project spending and marketing costs. GAAP operating income fell 22.9% to $1,135M and net income fell 24.6% to $781M against a year-ago quarter with $441M of interchange-settlement gains; adjusted operating income rose 29.1%. Cash fell to $3,534M from $5,488M on debt repayment with no buybacks. Target raised FY2026 sales-growth guidance to ~4% and expects EPS near the top of its $7.50-$8.50 range.

drivers.explanation: Net sales rose on 5.6% comparable sales growth (traffic +4.4%, digital +8.9%) across all six core merchandise categories, plus nearly 25% growth in advertising, membership and marketplace revenue.
Gross margin rate rose to 29.0% from 28.2% on improved supply-chain productivity, growth in advertising/non-merchandise revenue and lower markdown rates, partly offset by higher product costs.

GAAP operating income fell because the year-ago quarter included $593M of pretax interchange-fee settlement gains; SG&A rate rose to 21.9% on higher compensation, incentive pay, capital-project spending and marketing, partly offset by topline leverage.
EBIT's decline mirrors operating income's drop plus a smaller net other income figure ($15M vs $26M a year ago); the release does not discuss EBIT separately.
EBITDA fell in line with operating income's decline; depreciation and amortization rose only modestly to $685M from $655M, so it did not offset the profit drop.

Net income fell as GAAP operating and pretax earnings declined against the year-ago quarter's $441M after-tax interchange-settlement gain, partly offset by a lower 24.4% effective tax rate versus 25.0%.
EPS diluted fell in line with net income's 24.6% decline; diluted weighted shares fell only slightly (455.8M vs 456.5M), so per-share results tracked net income closely.

Management called results 'stronger than expected' with broad-based growth; the year-ago GAAP comparison is distorted by a one-time $441M interchange-settlement gain, and the company raised FY2026 sales-growth guidance while pointing EPS toward the high end of its existing range.
